# Vornik

> Local-first orchestration daemon for teams of AI agents. Vornik runs asynchronous projects, swarms, workflows, memory, approvals, companion delegation, and operator tooling on infrastructure you control.

Install: `curl -fsSL https://get.vornik.io | bash`  (Linux with rootless Podman recommended)

Repo: https://github.com/EaseIT-cz/vornik
Docs: https://docs.vornik.io

- [Self-healing workflow genome](https://docs.vornik.io/features/self-healing/): Workflows drift. A model changes, an upstream API gets slower, a prompt that used to work starts failing — and the failure rate or cost of a workflow creeps up. The self-healing genome is the loop that notices the...
- [Instinct layer](https://docs.vornik.io/features/instinct/): The instinct layer lets vornik learn from its own history. It mines the telemetry every task already produces, distils recurring patterns into confidence-scored instincts — "in situation T, action A held up" — and...
- [Authentication & access control](https://docs.vornik.io/features/auth/): vornik's control-plane API and UI can require authentication, and once a user is authenticated their role and project scope decide what they can see and do. This page covers turning auth on, the ways a request can be...
- [Memory & RAG](https://docs.vornik.io/features/memory-rag/): vornik can consolidate and semantically recall project memory so agents carry context forward across tasks, with caches that cut cost and latency. A policy-aware firewall governs what may enter that memory and what may...
- [Zero-egress / local-first execution](https://docs.vornik.io/features/zero-egress/): vornik is built to run agents that have no direct path to the internet. Each agent runs in its own rootless Podman container; in the zero-egress posture that container has no network device at all. Anything that...
- [Cluster topology and node roles](https://docs.vornik.io/features/cluster/): vornik can run as a single all-in-one daemon (the default) or as a multi-node cluster where each node takes a specialised role. Roles let you scale the worker tier independently of the UI/API tier and isolate public...
- [Forge — GitHub automation](https://docs.vornik.io/features/forge/): Forge connects a vornik project to a GitHub repository so that labelling an issue opens a pull request, and opening a pull request gets a review — done by your swarm, on your infrastructure. The defining property is...
- [Companion plugin](https://docs.vornik.io/features/companion/): The vornik companion connects your host LLM session to a running vornik daemon. It ships as a Claude Code plugin and as a Codex plugin; both use the same companion MCP endpoint and scoped key model. It gives you two...
- [Knowledge skills](https://docs.vornik.io/features/knowledge-skills/): A knowledge skill is a piece of reusable, instructional know-how — a troubleshooting flow, a non-obvious fix, a deploy/verify sequence — captured once and then applied automatically by future agent runs. It is the...
- [Control plane](https://docs.vornik.io/features/control-plane/): The control plane helps you operate vornik — troubleshoot, tune, and change configuration — instead of hand-editing YAML and reading raw logs. Its Phase-1 core is a human-gated proposal ledger: a suggested change (a...

- [Reference architecture](https://docs.vornik.io/reference/reference-architecture/): This page describes the expected shape of a healthy vornik deployment, so you can check an install against it. It is written to be *executable*: the validate-install companion skill reads this page, inspects a live...
- [Configuration reference](https://docs.vornik.io/reference/configuration/): vornik reads its configuration from config.yaml. The keys below are the customer-facing settings, by dotted YAML path. Where an environment variable overrides a key it is listed; an override wins over the file, and...
- [vornikctl CLI reference](https://docs.vornik.io/reference/vornikctl/): vornikctl inspects and controls a running vornik daemon.

## Benchmarks
- [Benchmarks](https://docs.vornik.io/benchmarks/): Vornik is measured, not asserted. This section states what we measure, how to reproduce it, and where Vornik loses.
- [Results by release](https://docs.vornik.io/benchmarks/results/): One row per release, per benchmark. Rows are never edited after a release ships — a regression is shown by the next row being worse, not by the previous row changing.
